question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity

$$
1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x={sech}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{2-2{tanh}^{4}⁡x}{1+{tanh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{1-{tanh}^{4}⁡x}{1+{tanh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{(1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x)(1+{tanh}^{2}⁡x)}{1+{tanh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{sech}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =2\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-2\operatorname{tanh}⁡0 \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+1}-2\cdot \frac{{e}^{0}-1}{{e}^{0}+1} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{2}^{2}-1}{{2}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
